review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the simp-relevant API in W1p/Basic.lean, W1p/Zero.lean, Multiplication.lean, VanishingBoundary.lean and SupercriticalMultiplication.lean, plus Mathlib's MemLp.coeFn_toLp. The one concrete gap is that W1p.value has no simp lemmas for addition or scalar multiplication. I did not flag the ae-equality lemmas (such as coeFn_sobolevEmbeddingL) as missing simp lemmas, because Mathlib's own coeFn_toLp is not simp. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim that the proposed lemmas compile or that simp's behaviour changes as described.

findings.problem: There is no canonical simp lemma `W1p.value (u + v) = W1p.value u + W1p.value v` (or the `smul` analogue), so this proof has to run the simp lemma `W1p.valueL_apply` backwards, going from `value` to `valueL`, in order to use `map_add`/`map_smul`. `W1p.valueL_apply` is `@[simp]` in the direction `valueL u = value u`, so this reverse rewrite goes against the simp set. The same detour appears elsewhere. Examples are W1p/Zero.lean (`simp only [← W1p.valueL_apply, ← W1p.gradientL_apply, map_add]`), Multiplication.lean (`have hvalue : ∀ w z : W1p mu Omega p, W1p.value (w + z) = ...` proved by `rw [← W1p.valueL_apply, map_add, ...]`), and line 403 of that file. Each of these re-proves the same local `hvalue` fact by hand.
findings.proposed_change: In W1p/Basic.lean, next to `W1p.valueL_apply`, add `@[simp] theorem W1p.value_add (u v : W1p mu Omega p) : W1p.value (u + v) = W1p.value u + W1p.value v`, with `value_smul` and `value_neg`/`value_sub`/`value_zero` alongside. Prove them by `simp only [← W1p.valueL_apply, map_add]`, or by `map_add W1p.valueL u v`. Add the matching `gradient_*` lemmas. Then `map_add'` and `map_smul'` here reduce to `simp only [Submodule.coe_add, W1p.value_add]; exact Lp.coeFn_add _ _`, and the `hvalue` helper proofs here and in Multiplication.lean can be dropped. The existing `value_add_ae` lemmas could then be derived from the Lp-level equalities.
findings.benefit: Callers get a normal form for values of sums and scalar multiples without reversing a simp lemma. The repeated `← valueL_apply, map_add` boilerplate disappears, and `simp` can push `value` through linear combinations of Sobolev functions.

evidence.excerpt: theorem W1p.valueL_apply (u : W1p mu Omega p) : W1p.valueL u = W1p.value u := (rfl)
simpa only [← W1p.valueL_apply, map_add] using Lp.coeFn_add (W1p.value u) (W1p.value v)

evidence.declaration: local hvalue in the multiplication construction
evidence.excerpt: have hvalue : ∀ w z : W1p mu Omega p, W1p.value (w + z) = W1p.value w + W1p.value z := by
simp only [← W1p.valueL_apply, ← W1p.gradientL_apply, map_add] <;> simp
